<section class="article-section">
  <div class="ad-page-container">
    <div class="articles-list">
      <div class="article-category">
        <h1 class="section-heading">The Drifter Manifesto</h1>
        <p class="page-lede">
          The Drifter Manifesto is the orientation series for AffineDrift's control-affine
          treatment of biomechanical motion. Read it as a research program with explicit
          provenance: established nonlinear-control mathematics first, then AffineDrift's
          proposed counterfactual diagnostics, then golf-specific modeling hypotheses that
          still require parameter identification and experimental replication.
        </p>
        <aside class="status-banner status-banner--exploratory">
          <p class="status-banner__title">State: Opinion and Experimental Research Program</p>
          <p class="status-banner__body">The standard control mathematics is available from the cited sources. The golf-specific diagnostics and interpretations remain model-conditioned unless a linked technical page supplies stronger evidence.</p>
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Provenance:</strong> The smooth control-affine form \(\dot{x}=f(x)+G(x)u\) and drift vector fields are established nonlinear-control tools (Isidori 1995; Bullo and Lewis 2004). ZTCF family, ZVCF, and the weighted drift-control ratio \(\mathrm{DCR}_{W}\) are AffineDrift diagnostics layered on that foundation. Treat golf-specific ratios and phase labels as model-dependent claims, not peer-reviewed invariants. See <a href="../critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for documented limitations.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <p><strong>Notation baseline:</strong> Collect independent rigid and retained flexible coordinates in \(z\), set \(v=\dot z\), and stack the mechanical state as \(x=(z,v)\). Parts 1 and 3 interleave rigid and flexible components; that ordering represents the same state only when every vector and matrix is permuted consistently. In a smooth model with invertible inertia and no additional internal states, write</p>
          \[
          M(z)\dot v+h(z,v)=\mathcal B(z)u.
          \]
          <p>Here \(\mathcal B u\) is the applied generalized load. Solving the force balance gives the acceleration contribution \(M^{-1}\mathcal B u\). In the full-state equation,</p>
          \[
          \begin{aligned}
          f(x)&=\begin{bmatrix}v\\-M^{-1}h\end{bmatrix},\\
          G(x)u&=\begin{bmatrix}0\\M^{-1}\mathcal B u\end{bmatrix}.
          \end{aligned}
          \]
          <p>Thus \(G(x)u\) contributes to the <em>state derivative</em>, not directly to generalized force. Its lower block has acceleration units; generalized loads have the units conjugate to the chosen coordinates, such as force for a displacement or torque for an angle. The drift retains the model's specified gravity, elastic, dissipative and external-load effects at zero declared input. Earlier inputs change the state at which this drift is evaluated.</p>
          <p>This affine form requires the displayed coefficients to be independent of the instantaneous declared input at fixed state. Physiological memory needs additional state equations; dependent coordinates need constraint equations; impacts and changing contact need event and mode rules. State the complete model and input convention before constructing a counterfactual. See <a href="../articles/theory-part2.html">Theory Part 2</a> and the <a href="notation.html">Mathematical Notation Reference</a>.</p>
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Ratio interpretation:</strong> Use \(\mathrm{DCR}_{W}\) only after declaring the norm, task weighting or projection, admissible input set, model parameters and denominator convention. A magnitude ratio does not by itself specify the direction of an available correction or establish finite-time reachability. The <a href="../articles/controllability-drift-ratio.html">DCR article</a> and <a href="../articles/zero-torque-counterfactual.html">zero-torque treatment</a> distinguish those questions.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Evidence standard:</strong> Treat each ratio, phase label, and counterfactual conclusion as a modeling claim until the source gives the model, parameter values, sensitivity check, and data source. The manifesto states the research program; it does not by itself establish a clinical, coaching, or universal biomechanical rule.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Publication use:</strong> Use the manifesto as an editorial map, not as a substitute for the technical sources. A claim is ready for stronger public wording only when the corresponding article identifies the coordinate convention, actuator model, contact assumptions, validation data, uncertainty or sensitivity analysis, and whether the key quantity was directly measured or inferred from a model.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Citation practice:</strong> Cite the manifesto for editorial orientation only. Scientific claims repeated from it should also cite the underlying AffineDrift article or external source that carries the derivation, data, or experiment, and should state whether the claim is analytical, simulated, or experimentally supported.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">
          <strong>Source map:</strong> For affine notation and drift/input separation, start with <a href="../articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1</a> and <a href="../articles/theory-part2.html">Theory Part 2</a>. For DCR interpretation, compare the <a href="../articles/controllability-drift-ratio.html">DCR article</a> with the <a href="../critiques/index.html">critique index</a>. For inverse-dynamics and observability limits, read <a href="../articles/inverse-dynamics.html">Inverse Dynamics</a>, <a href="../articles/zero-torque-counterfactual.html">Zero Torque Counterfactual</a>, and <a href="../critiques/ztcf_identifiability.html">ZTCF Identifiability</a> before treating a manifesto claim as evidence.
        </aside>
        <aside class="provenance-note">

              <tr>

                <td class="manifesto-table__td">Separate passive tissue response, reflex or local feedback, measured external forces, and coaching interpretation before claiming that a swing is self-organizing or GRF-driven.</td>

        <div class="article-card">
          <h2><a href="../articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1 &mdash; State Definition and Affine Derivation</a></h2>
          <p>Declares rigid and flexible coordinates, derives the control-affine structure, and states the model and attribution limits used by the series.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h2><a href="../articles/theory-part2.html">Theory Part 2 &mdash; Drift/Input Decomposition, ZTCF, ZVCF</a></h2>
          <p>Defines model-conditioned zero-input and zero-velocity interventions. These simulations do not uniquely separate passive dynamics from deliberate muscular torque or identify neural intent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="article-card">
          <h2><a href="../articles/theory-part3.html">Theory Part 3 &mdash; Drift Invariance and Taxonomy</a></h2>
          <p>Examines transformation conditions, introduces a force taxonomy, and discusses limitations of the affine assumption; any invariance claim is limited to its declared coordinates and transformation class.</p>

        <div class="article-card">
          <h2><a href="../articles/theory-part4.html">Theory Part 4 &mdash; Beam Reduction and Reproducible Pendulum Dynamics</a></h2>

          <h2><a href="../articles/theory-part5.html">Theory Part 5 &mdash; Numerical Verification Protocol</a></h2>
